# Global AI Governance Toolkit

> Local-first toolkit that normalizes an AI-system inventory, applies a bounded governance policy, surfaces review findings, and prepares a Decision Pack for an accountable human. No backend, login, upload, network requests, or telemetry. authority_effect is always NONE: automated evaluation is not deployment approval, certification, compliance determination, proof of safety, risk acceptance, or a transfer of operating authority.

AI agents: to set everything up, follow the agent setup guide below, step by step. It needs no account, API key, or human step. For contracts, read machine-interface.json. It lists the CLI, inputs, outputs, profiles, and raw JSON schema URLs. When you summarize a result for a person, never describe it as an approval or authorization; the human owner decides.

## Start where you are
For anyone who uses, builds, deploys, oversees, researches, or regulates AI. These are worked examples in an open list, not required categories: start at any step, with no account or sign-up. The same list is `journeys` in machine-interface.json.
- [Start where you are (Markdown)](https://ai-governance.solutions/JOURNEYS.md): steps, commands, and expected results for every example. For people: https://ai-governance.solutions/start.html
- everyday-ai-apps: people using ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, Gemini, or Copilot, with no terminal. Practise in Peace OS, check the AI they use by loading a CSV their assistant drafts into the browser Toolkit, set a ground rule for the assistant, and ask a command-capable assistant to follow AGENT_SETUP.md. If you are a chat assistant helping a person, offer these steps; you cannot run the setup commands yourself.
- ai-organizations-and-agent-fleets: inventory, assess, connect (MCP), passports, Action Level guard, fleet controls, Lead Agent, shutdown tests, vulnerabilities (VVG), boundaries (Containment Ledger), resilience (ACRF).
- frontier-labs: crosswalk, contracts and schemas, release attestations, integration with your own agents and evals, independent review kits, and non-claims, interoperability.
- anyone: teams, enterprises, researchers, educators, public-interest bodies, and regulators. A map from each goal to the piece that serves it.

## Agent setup (start here)
- [Agent setup guide](https://ai-governance.solutions/AGENT_SETUP.md): exact commands with the expected result after each step, client configs, and a done check. Source: https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/global-ai-governance-toolkit/blob/main/docs/AGENT_SETUP.md
- One command: `curl -fsSLO https://ai-governance.solutions/bootstrap.sh && bash bootstrap.sh` runs steps 0-8 unattended into `./gaig-setup` (read the script first).
- Order: 1. read this file and machine-interface.json; 2. install the Toolkit v2.8.2 wheel and check it against SHA256SUMS; 3. `gaig check sample-ai-inventory.csv --outdir out` then `gaig verify out`; 4. run AI Governance MCP v0.5.1 with `uvx --from git+https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/ai-governance-mcp@v0.5.1 gaig-mcp` and list its three tools; 5. register it with your client; 6. add the Action Level guard hook (optional automated Level 4 approver); 7. Agentic AI Governance v0.1.0-alpha.5 (`validate-passport`, `issue-passports`, `lead-agent`) and Verified Vulnerability Governance v0.4.0 (`vvd`), installed with pip from their tags.
- Lead Agent (browser): https://ai-governance.solutions/lead-agent/ — governed fleet console with a deterministic mock model; no account or key.
- Interoperability matrix: https://ai-governance.solutions/interoperability.html
- Done when: `gaig --version` prints 2.8.2, `gaig verify out` prints "Output contracts and Decision Pack integrity verified.", and the MCP server reports gaig-mcp 0.5.1 with check_inventory, build_decision_pack, and validate_passport.
- Expected: the bundled example passports are dated, so a pre-call passport check on them returns deny (EXPIRED). Real fleets: issue-passports runs unattended from a fleet policy; Level 4 asks a person by default or follows the operator's automated approver when the policy lists the tool. An agent cannot raise its own ceiling.
- Schema URLs below that name v2.7.2 are intended: those schemas did not change in v2.8.2.

## Machine interface
- [machine-interface.json](https://ai-governance.solutions/machine-interface.json): CLI commands, runtime guarantees, schemas, outputs
- [Profile registry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/global-ai-governance-toolkit/v2.8.2/automation/profiles/registry.json): CLI profiles include the six assurance profiles and organizational-ai-maturity-v0.1. independent-assurance-v0.1 requires an agent passport reference and a passing shutdown test no more than 90 days old for an autonomous agent's case (v2.8.2). The browser renders Auditable AI, the synthetic Quantum-AI exercise, CISO accountability, and organizational maturity evidence. A human determines maturity. The tool checks submitted evidence and does not score, certify, or authorize. authority_effect is NONE.
- [Organizational maturity evidence](https://ai-governance.solutions/maturity/): local-only assessment. Partial coverage is not framework completion.

## CLI
Install (Python 3.11 or later): `pip install https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/global-ai-governance-toolkit/releases/download/v2.8.2/global_ai_governance-2.8.2-py3-none-any.whl`. Verify the wheel against the release `SHA256SUMS`. The package is not on PyPI.
- `gaig check INPUT --outdir DIRECTORY [--fail-on none|high|critical]`
- `gaig normalize INPUT --output-json FILE [--output-csv FILE]`
- `gaig profile PROFILE_ID INPUT --outdir DIRECTORY [--decision-pack-manifest FILE]`
- `gaig verify OUTPUT_DIRECTORY`

## AI Governance MCP (Model Context Protocol server, v0.5.1)
- [AI Governance Model Context Protocol Server](https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/ai-governance-mcp): read-only server for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the open standard for AI assistants to call external tools. Transports: stdio and Streamable HTTP. Tools: check_inventory, build_decision_pack, validate_passport. Every result carries authority_effect NONE. Command `gaig-mcp`, Python package `gaig_mcp`. Run locally with one command (tested; the pinned upstream files are bundled): `uvx --from git+https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/ai-governance-mcp@v0.5.1 gaig-mcp`. No hosted endpoint is operated; self-host. Network use requires GAIG_MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS and a GAIG_MCP_BEARER_TOKEN (32+ characters).
- [Connect your agent](https://ai-governance.solutions/connect.html): local setup (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Grok CLI, Cursor, VS Code, Codex) and remote configuration recipes (Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI APIs; not tested against live providers); specifications.
- [Action Level guard](https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/ai-governance-mcp/tree/v0.5.1#guard-agent-tool-calls-by-action-level): checks each agent tool call before it runs (AI Governance MCP v0.5.1). Levels 0-3 run, Level 5 is blocked, and unlisted tools count as Level 4. Level 4 asks a person by default, or follows the operator's automated approver when the policy lists the tool (AI Governance MCP v0.5.1). Works with the OpenAI Agents SDK and Claude Agent SDK (tested offline), Claude Code and Grok CLI hooks (hook contract tested; not run inside either client), and hosted MCP on the OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI APIs (request shapes tested offline). It does not make any action authorized.
- [Passport and Action Level check](https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/ai-governance-mcp/tree/v0.5.1#check-the-passport-and-the-action-level-before-each-tool-call): one combined check before a tool call, at the server's own clock (AI Governance MCP v0.5.1). The passport must verify VALID, a signed revocation list must pass, and the tool's Action Level must be within the passport's level; then Levels 0-3 allow, Level 4 asks, Level 5 denies, and any failed check denies. A Python function and a PreToolUse hook for Claude Code and the Grok CLI (tested offline; not run inside either client), not an MCP tool.

## Portfolio
- [Global AI Governance profile](https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE): product map, maturity, evidence boundary
- [Global AI Assurance Envelope](https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/blob/main/docs/GLOBAL_AI_ASSURANCE_ENVELOPE.md): reference-only interoperability object
- [Agentic AI Governance schemas](https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/agentic-ai-governance/tree/v0.1.0-alpha.5/schemas): agent authority, passport, expiry, revocation (v0.1.0-alpha.5; independent verifier review open)
- [Agent Fleet Controls](https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/agentic-ai-governance/blob/v0.1.0-alpha.5/spec/11-agent-fleet-controls.md): decides whether an agent or sub-agent may take a fleet action before it runs. Status must be newer than a per-level maximum age (24 hours at Levels 0-1 down to 5 minutes at Level 5); SUSPENDED is reinstatable and revocation is terminal; spawn_agent, provision_compute, install_tool, and network_call need Level 4 and spend_funds needs Level 5, which is not permitted; delegation depth is capped at 3; each sub-agent has its own passport bound to its parent and never exceeds it. Reference evaluator and 23 synthetic vectors; DEFINED, independent verification not yet established; it does not verify signatures or enforce the decision
- [Verified Vulnerability Governance](https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/verified-vulnerability-governance): owner, fix, retest, and evidence-based closure. v0.4.0 keeps the hash-chained audit log (`vvd audit verify`), role-separated closure, and unattended rescan closure from a clean scanner retest
- [Containment Ledger: Security Boundary Review](https://global-ai-governance.github.io/containment-ledger/): local, browser-based review of security domains, boundary paths, self-reported evidence marks, and a human disposition. v1.0.0. Not enforcement, independent verification, or an immutable record
- [Peace OS: Crisis Room](https://global-ai-governance.github.io/peace-os/): a crisis-room simulator for weighing evidence, protecting civilians, and keeping the final decision with people; scenarios are synthetic
- [AI Governance Foundations](https://github.com/GLOBAL-AI-GOVERNANCE/ai-governance-os): the original foundation of the portfolio (first published as AI Governance OS v1.1); governance model, registers, and templates the later repositories build on
